remedies.title: Replace the self-referential analytic check with a two-interpretation differential check
remedies.rationale: The traces show the current check is information-free: 11/11 tasks report rel.diff <= 1e-15 while 9/11 miss the graded volume, up to 46.9%. The check confirms arithmetic, which was never the failure mode; every observed miss was an interpretation choice (which axial extent shaft_length names, whether flange_thickness exists, where the elbow legs start) that the single-model check cannot see.
remedies.whyWorks: Forcing the agent to enumerate the admissible readings of every ambiguous parameter and compute the volume under each turns a self-confirming comparison into a discriminating one: when two readings differ by more than the ~0.6% volume tolerance the agent is made aware that a choice exists, must state it explicitly, and can select on external grounds (family convention, catalogue plausibility) instead of silently locking in the first reading it formed.

Before the existing text, insert a step A0: 'Ambiguity enumeration. List every key parameter whose geometric meaning admits more than one reading (which axial extent a length names; whether a stated diameter is at the root, pitch or tip; whether an overlapping feature is additive or included). For each, write out BOTH readings and the resulting total volume.'

Add: 'If two readings differ by more than 0.5% in volume, you have a real decision, not an arithmetic task. State the decision and its ground in your final message. Do NOT let the analytic match to your own chosen reading stand in for evidence that the reading is correct.'

Amend the existing sentence 'Any relative difference above 0.1% must be explained exactly' with: 'This check proves your script implements your model. It does NOT prove your model matches the part. It cannot fail if your arithmetic is right, so a passing result is not evidence of correctness.'

remedies.title: Publish the grading tolerances to the agent so it can triage effort
remedies.rationale: The reward data shows the volume sub-metric reaches zero at roughly 0.6% relative difference (0.231% scored 0.637, 0.273% scored 0.563, 2.231% scored 0.000) while surface area tolerates roughly ten times more (2.190% still scored 0.660). The playbook instead states a uniform 'volume to 0.1% and surface area to 1%', which understates how brittle volume is and overstates how brittle area is, so the agent cannot tell that a 2% volume miss is a total loss.
remedies.whyWorks: Stating the real shape of the scoring function converts an invisible cliff into a budget the agent can reason about: it learns that any volume discrepancy above roughly half a percent forfeits the largest single sub-metric outright, which raises the priority of resolving interpretation ambiguity above the cosmetic work the traces show it spending turns on.

State that geometry_similarity is a weighted blend dominated by surface_area and volume, with bounding box and surface-type mix contributing less.

State the observed tolerance bands: volume sub-score falls to zero near 0.6% relative difference; surface area near 6%; treat 0.1% volume as the working target and anything above 0.5% as a failed task.

remedies.title: Capture verifier stdout and stderr so a zero score is attributable
remedies.rationale: The trial retains reward.json and a one-line reward.txt but an empty test-stdout.txt, so the single most damaging result in the slice — a perfect part scored zero — cannot be traced to a cause from the artifacts. remedies.whyWorks: Persisting the verifier's stdout and stderr, plus the exact spec payload it scored against, makes the two invocations directly comparable: a genuine geometry defect leaves a per-parameter mismatch table, whereas a harness failure leaves an exception or an empty measurement set. That distinction is currently unavailable and is what forces manual re-grading.

remedies.title: Flag geometry-perfect / spec-zero results as suspect before accepting the score
remedies.rationale: Because the task score is the harmonic mean of the two sub-metrics, a spurious spec zero discards a fully correct answer outright — this single trial cost the full point on a task the baseline scored 1.0. The combination geometry_similarity=1.000 with cad_spec_consistency=0.000 is self-contradictory and mechanically detectable.
remedies.whyWorks: Geometry similarity of exactly 1.000 means the answer and the reference are the same shape, so any parameter the checker can measure on one it measures identically on the other; a spec rate of 0.000 in that situation is impossible on the merits and can only come from the scoring path. Detecting the contradiction automatically routes the trial to a re-grade instead of silently banking a zero.

remedies.title: Keep a per-task interpretation ledger and feed the winning reading back into the prompt
remedies.rationale: Four tasks previously scored 1.0 came back at 0.167, 0.589, 0.626 and 0.000 while three others improved, so the dominant term in the slice score is which reading the agent happens to form, not whether it can build the part. The traces show the decision is made explicitly and in prose every time, which means it is capturable.
remedies.whyWorks: Recording the interpretation alongside the score turns an independent draw into a ratchet: a task that has scored 1.0 gets its winning reading pinned into the next prompt so the agent reproduces rather than re-derives it, and a task that scored poorly gets its losing reading recorded as one to avoid. This directly removes the variance without needing to solve the underlying ambiguity.

remedies.title: Gate submission on a regression check against the recorded best score
remedies.rationale: The run silently accepted four regressions from a recorded 1.0, including one to 0.000, with no signal that a better answer for those tasks already existed. The baseline scores are already stored in final_run_scores.json, so the comparison costs nothing.
remedies.whyWorks: Comparing each new trial against the recorded best for that task surfaces regressions at the moment they happen instead of at post-hoc analysis time, letting the run retry or retain the better answer rather than banking the worse one. It also isolates genuine capability gaps — tasks that have never scored well — from variance on tasks already solved.
